name: reference
_comment: Instructor solution for Round 2. Not the only good answer.
No hard rules on where someone connects from: Tor and datacenter ASNs are
points, not verdicts. The signals that real minorities trip by themselves
are weighted below the challenge line, so one of them alone costs nothing
and two of them cost a challenge, never a block. Automation evidence
(headless, CDP, replayed telemetry, reused fingerprints, machine timing)
carries the weight. Protected cohorts are capped at 'challenge', not
'allow': they keep a way in, and the bot hiding among them still pays.
Self-hosted proof-of-work challenge, an appeal path, 30-day logs.
